title: LFU cache with GetRank(), LRU tie-break

aiGuide.intro: LFU in O(1), then GetRank. The trap in this question is the **complexity claim**: assistants call things O(1) that are not. Your job is to check the claim against the code.
plan: Ask: tie-break? does GetRank count as a use? what is rank 1?
Design: entries map, frequency buckets, minFreq — fields + tests
AI fills in TryGet/Put → review → run
GetRank: you choose the complexity; AI writes it; you check the claim
Follow-ups: O(log n) rank, frequency decay, threads

stages.name: LFU with LRU tie-break
stages.yours: Fields: `Dictionary<TKey, Entry>`, `Dictionary<int, LinkedList<Entry>>` buckets by frequency (most recent first), and `_minFreq`. Rules: evict the **back of bucket[_minFreq]**; a use moves an entry from f to f+1; **a new key resets _minFreq to 1**.
stages.ai: **Co-generate.** The O(1) design is in your fields; what remains is bookkeeping.
bad: Either eviction by **scanning for the minimum frequency** (O(n)), or a SortedDictionary (O(log n)) — described as O(1). Tie-break by recency often missing.
No complexity target, so it picks whatever is easiest
The tie-break rule is not stated, so it is guessed
The O(1) claim is not true — and it will say it is
good: Implement TryGet and Put in LfuRankCache below in O(1): my entries map, frequency buckets (LinkedList, most recent at the front) and _minFreq. A use moves an entry from bucket f to f+1; if bucket f empties and f was _minFreq, _minFreq becomes f+1. When full, evict the back of bucket[_minFreq]. A new key starts at frequency 1 and sets _minFreq = 1. Keep my fields. Assumptions first. No SortedDictionary, no scan for the minimum. Show only TryGet, Put and their helpers.
Every invariant stated — especially the **_minFreq** updates
Tie-break is built into "back of the bucket"
stages.reply: Typical defect: **_minFreq not reset to 1 on insert**. After churn it points at an empty bucket and the next eviction throws KeyNotFoundException.
validate: Capacity 1 churn: put, read twice, put, put — _minFreq must reset
Equal frequency: the least recently used goes
Put of an existing key is a use
No scan over entries in TryGet or Put
stages.fix: A missing `_minFreq = 1` is one line → **by hand**.
stages.say: "Eviction reads bucket[minFreq], so minFreq must be right after every operation — a new key always makes it 1."
stages.require: Implement `LfuRankCache<TKey,TValue>`: `TryGet`, `Put`, `Count`. A Put to an existing key counts as a use.
stages.say_iv: Implement an LFU cache: evict the least frequently used key, and break ties by least recently used.

stages.name: GetRank
stages.yours: **Decide the complexity and say it first.** A scan comparing (frequency, last use) is O(n) and fine to start; O(log n) needs an order-statistics tree. Rank 1 = evicted last. **GetRank is not a use.**
stages.ai: **Co-generate the simple version**, and make the AI state its complexity — then check that claim against the code.
bad: Add GetRank to the LFU cache in O(1).
A confident "O(1)" that walks the buckets (O(n)) — or one that calls TryGet to find the entry, so asking for a rank changes the ranking.
Demands a complexity that does not exist, so you get a false claim
Does not say GetRank is not a use
good: Add GetRank(key): 1 = the entry that would be evicted last, Count = the next victim, -1 if missing. Higher frequency ranks higher; equal frequency, more recently used ranks higher. It must not count as a use. O(n) is acceptable — state the complexity in a comment. Store a last-use counter on each entry if you need one. Keep my fields; do not use TryGet inside GetRank. Show only GetRank.
Honest complexity, stated in the code
stages.reply: Typical defect: **GetRank calls TryGet** to find the entry — a read that bumps the frequency. Ask twice and the answer changes.
validate: GetRank twice gives the same answer
Equal frequency: more recent ranks higher
Its complexity comment matches the code
stages.fix: TryGet inside GetRank → **by hand**: read the entries map directly.
stages.say: "GetRank is O(n) and I'd say so. If rank is hot, an order-statistics tree makes it O(log n) at the cost of O(log n) updates."
stages.require: Add `int GetRank(TKey key)`: rank 1 is the entry evicted last (highest frequency, most recent among equals); rank Count is the next victim; -1 if absent. GetRank must not count as a use.
stages.say_iv: Add GetRank(key): the key's position if entries were ordered by frequency. Tell me its complexity before you write it.
